AbstractText.Label: OBJECTIVE
AbstractText.content: Direct electrical stimulation (DES) is a clinical gold standard for human brain mapping and readily evokes conscious percepts, yet the neurophysiological changes underlying these percepts are not well understood.

AbstractText.Label: APPROACH
AbstractText.content: To determine the neural correlates of DES, we stimulated the somatosensory cortex of ten human participants at frequency-amplitude combinations that both elicited and failed to elicit conscious percepts, meanwhile recording neural activity directly surrounding the stimulation site. We then compared the neural activity of perceived trials to that of non-perceived trials.

AbstractText.Label: MAIN RESULTS
AbstractText.content: We found that stimulation evokes distributed high gamma activity, which correlates with conscious perception better than stimulation parameters themselves.

AbstractText.Label: SIGNIFICANCE
AbstractText.content: Our findings suggest that high gamma activity is a reliable biomarker for perception evoked by both natural and electrical stimuli.
